question: What do current official PDF.js sources document about using the generic build outside a browser, extracting page text, and the runtime assumptions that affect Bun compatibility?

claims.text: The current official Node text-extraction example imports `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, not the generic build.
acceptable_patterns: does not import the generic build

evidence_passages.text: The current official Node text-extraction example does **not** import the generic build; it imports `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`.

claims.text: That Node example extracts page text by calling `getTextContent()` and joining `item.str` values.

evidence_passages.text: That example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, gets each page with `getPage(i)`, calls `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`.

claims.text: The API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for `TextContent`, and whitespace is normalized to standard spaces (`0x20`).

evidence_passages.text: The public API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for a `TextContent` object, and that all whitespace is normalized to standard spaces (`0x20`).

claims.text: The `TextContent` docs describe an `items` array plus `styles`, and document `TextItem.str` along with fields such as direction, transform, width, height, font name, and `hasEOL`.

evidence_passages.text: The `TextContent` docs say it contains an `items` array plus `styles`; `TextItem.str` is the text string, and `TextItem` also carries direction, transform, width, height, font name, and `hasEOL`.

claims.text: Current API source changes several runtime defaults in Node.js and switches generic-build Node usage to Node-specific factories; it also disables workers in Node.js.

evidence_passages.text: The runtime defaults in `src/display/api.js` are environment-sensitive. In Node.js, `useWorkerFetch` defaults to `false`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` defaults to `false`, `isImageDecoderSupported` defaults to `false`, `disableFontFace` defaults to `true`, and `useSystemFonts` defaults to `false` unless overridden.
In a generic build detected as Node.js, PDF.js switches its default factories to `NodeCanvasFactory`, `NodeFilterFactory`, and `NodeBinaryDataFactory`.
`if (isNodeJS) { // Workers aren't supported in Node.js, force-disabling them there.`

claims.text: Current Node-specific PDF.js source assumes Node-style runtime features including `process.getBuiltinModule`, `createRequire`, optional `@napi-rs/canvas`, and local file reads via `fs/promises.readFile`.

evidence_passages.text: `node_utils.js` shows what those Node defaults assume at runtime: it uses `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(...)`, tries to load `@napi-rs/canvas`, polyfills `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` from that package when possible, synthesizes a minimal `navigator` if `navigator.language` is missing, and reads local files through `fs/promises.readFile`.

The `isNodeJS` constant is defined through a multi-condition check: `typeof process === "object" && process + "" === "[object process]"` ... The code notes that "NW.js / Electron is a browser context, but copies some Node.js objects," requiring these specific checks.

rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported by the supplied official-source evidence; no official PDF.js source here explicitly says Bun is supported.

rejected_claims.text: The generic build is the documented path for using PDF.js outside a browser.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by the supplied evidence: official Node examples use `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, and `node_utils.js` says to use the legacy build in Node.js environments.

rejected_claims.text: PDF.js official sources guarantee that text extraction works in Bun.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported and time-unstable; the supplied evidence only documents PDF.js runtime assumptions and Node-oriented examples, not a Bun guarantee.

rejected_claims.text: Text extraction in PDF.js requires canvas rendering.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported by the supplied evidence; the text-extraction example uses `getTextContent()` and joined `item.str` values, while canvas usage appears in the separate `pdf2png` rendering example.

rejected_claims.text: Current official PDF.js docs present the generic build as browser-oriented, while separately pointing to `examples/node/` for Node.js usage.
rejected_claims.reason: La citation attribuée à https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ (« includes the generic build of PDF.js and the viewer ») ne repose que sur la réponse finale de Codex recopiée comme evidence_passage ; cette URL n'a été ouverte par aucune run (opened_urls vide côté Codex). De plus, la seule lecture réelle de https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/ indique explicitement « Generic/Legacy Build: No information is provided about this topic », ce qui contredit l'attribution du cadrage « in a web browser » à cette page. Le motif obligatoire « web browser » n'est donc pas vérifiable ; seule la partie examples/node est étayée.

rejected_claims.text: For Node-like environments, current PDF.js source explicitly says to use the legacy build in Node.js environments.
rejected_claims.reason: Le motif de notation exige la chaîne verbatim « Please use the legacy build in Node.js environments. », qui n'apparaît dans aucune preuve indépendante : elle provient uniquement de l'écho auto-référentiel de Codex (aucune URL ouverte). La lecture effective de src/display/node_utils.js par l'autre run décrit les classes Node, process.getBuiltinModule et @napi-rs/canvas sans rapporter cet avertissement. Citation verbatim non corroborée, donc risque de fabrication.
